Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

I'm Professor Ananda, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering.

Key details

  • Today, we are going to see the semiconductor diode characteristics and parameters and with some numericals.
  • As we look at the forward bias here, initially for the applied voltage, the diode was off, and at particular voltage of Vf, the current start increasing.
  • Then, we also come to another parameter called forward current rating.
  • The forward current rating, which is I.
  • It's the maximum current at which the diode starts conducting.
  • It depends on the voltage at which the diode is on.
  • So the current can vary based on the device, because it depends on the fabrication of the device.
  • Then the maximum power expression P is equal to V into I.
  • The first is breakdown voltage.
  • Until there is a breakdown, there is a leakage current flowing, which is a reverse saturation current, which is less than the reverse saturation current, which is called as a leakage current.
  • We need to remember this.
  • Then, the reverse saturation current is this region, where the diode start conducting even with the reverse bias.
  • That happens at a reverse bias voltage.
  • It could vary based on the device.
  • It could be five volts reverse saturation current.
  • That depends on the fabrication again.
  • Then we also need to calculate what the peak inverse voltage, the voltage at which the device starts conducting, which is a peak inverse voltage rating.
  • And the diode representation symbol is this, where it looks like an arrow lying here.
  • The arrow indicate the conventional current flow from P region to N region.
  • Next, we also learn here the diode current expression or the Shockley's current equation.
  • When Vd is positive, we represent Id is equal to minus Is.
  • When Vd is negative, we represent Id is equal to minus Is.
  • When Vd is positive, we represent Id is approximately equal to Is into E to the power of qVd by NmkBT, where Id and Vd are the diode current and voltage respectively, where q is the charge of the electron, where eta is the ideality factor, where eta N is equal to one for indirect semiconductor like silicon, germanium, et cetera.
  • For a direct semiconductor, N is equal to two, where gallium arsenide, if you use gallium arsenide and indium phosphate.
  • Where k is the Boltzmann constant, T is the temperature in Kelvin.
  • We are going to use these k and the q values.
  • Where the kT by q is also called as a thermal voltage, where kT by q is equal to 25.9 millivolts.
  • At a temperature 27 degrees centigrade, a common temperature for a component in an enclosed operating system, determine the thermal voltage.
  • As we know the thermal voltage, how to calculate?
  • VT is equal to kT by q, where we need to calculate the T here.

Example or application from the lecture

  • The Shockley's equation is also called as a diode equation, help us to determine the current at the given temperature, knowing the diode voltage and saturation current.
  • That is given by Id is equal to Is into qVd by NqT minus one.
  • Then, k is the Boltzmann constant given by value.
